title: All known cognitive agents are collective intelligences made of agential parts

fields.label: Label
fields.value: All known cognitive agents are collective intelligences made of agential parts

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Every known cognitive agent is a collective intelligence: biological agents are made of parts (cells and other components) that are themselves agents in important ways, and there is no truly indivisible cognitive being.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2022, Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds › Introduction

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: All known cognitive agents are collective intelligences, because we are all made of parts; biological agents in particular are not just structurally modular, but made of parts that are themselves agents in important ways.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds”, Frontiers in systems neuroscience (2022), doi:10.3389/fnsys.2022.768201; section “Introduction”. Scope: All known cognitive agents, especially multicellular organisms

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2022-tame-01: not-empirically-resolvable, resolvability 0.16

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Structural compositionality is observable, but the assertion that all parts are agential in an important sense depends on TAME's conceptual vocabulary. Plausible observations do not cleanly distinguish the claim from narrower, non-agential descriptions.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: No non-circular dataset can enumerate every known cognitive agent while also deciding whether each component is an agent 'in important ways' under a definition independent of the claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The universal scope cannot be sampled adequately.

Agent and collective intelligence are definition-dependent.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.05
operationalizability: 0.2
discriminating power: 0.12
data existence: 0.2
analysis feasibility: 0.25

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Biological cognitive systems are structurally made of parts, which is true by anatomy and does not need a dataset. Calling those parts agents, and concluding there is no indivisible cognitive being, does not add an observation that would distinguish the claim from a non-agential parts list. The universal wording is fixed by the definition in use.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: A census of cognitive systems would need a part to count as an agent by a criterion that could fail; under the claim's usage, any functional part can be counted as an agent.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value: 'Agent in important ways' can be applied to whatever parts a system has, so no catalog of organisms yields a refuting case.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.05
operationalizability: 0.15
data existence: 0.05
discriminating power: 0.1
analysis feasibility: 0.1
